clue.text: Animals from a cold area in The Sound of Music setting

indicators.note: in says the short pieces sit inside the mountain range

parts.note: the musical The Sound of Music is set in the Austrian Alps
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Some cold-climate creatures are spotted in the mountain scenery of a famous musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpacas are domesticated South American camelids, kept as livestock for wool.

clue.text: Bogey's mate is playing song

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played about with, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: the possessive here keeps its S as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: Humphrey Bogart's pal Sam is at the piano performing a tune, as in Casablanca.
explanation.walkthrough: Bogey is Humphrey Bogart, and his mate Sam plays this very song in Casablanca, so the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the classic standard that Dooley Wilson sings at Rick's Café in the film Casablanca.

clue.text: Place provided by school governors changed by this?

parts.note: to put something is to place it

explanation.surface: Somewhere provided by a school's board, with the governors replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School governors' looks like one phrase, but school gives SCH and governors belongs to the definition: a coup changes those who govern.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup d'état overthrows the rulers of a state, replacing its government by force.

clue.text: Band of gold in furniture for officers

indicators.note: in places the heraldic gold inside the pieces of furniture

parts.note: commodes are chests of drawers or chair-like pieces of furniture
OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A wedding ring sits in some furniture meant for military officers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Commodores were also a soul band, so 'Band' hints at the answer too; the definition used is officers, naval ranks above captain.
explanation.definitionFit: Commodore is a naval rank, so these are senior officers in a navy.

clue.text: Winner of Nobel Prize climbing a tree

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the word reads upwards, so it is turned round

parts.note: Albert Camus won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1957

explanation.surface: A laureate is shinning up a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumac is a shrub or small tree of the genus Rhus.

clue.text: Medusa's snakes taken upon oneself

indicators.note: snakes as a verb means winds about, signalling a rearrangement of the letters

parts.note: the possessive keeps its S as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: The Gorgon Medusa's serpent hair is taken on by someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Medusa had snakes for hair, so 'snakes' reads as a noun; it is a verb telling you to twist her name.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume a duty or role is to take it on yourself.

clue.text: Unaccompanied, a top lady of jazz without piano

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the other pieces go round the piano letter

parts.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle
Ella Fitzgerald, the First Lady of Song, was a jazz singer
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A leading female jazz singer performs without any piano backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking, but in its older sense it means outside: the pieces wrap around the piano letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing a cappella means singing with no instrumental accompaniment.

clue.text: Transport announced for butcher

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the word for transport is heard rather than written

parts.note: a sleigh is a sledge used for transport over snow

explanation.surface: A vehicle is publicly declared for a meat trader.
explanation.definitionFit: To butcher people is to slaughter or kill them brutally.

clue.text: Lavender planted in battle for girl

indicators.note: planted in says one piece is set inside another

parts.note: the Battles of the Marne were fought in France in the First World War
Ian Lavender was an actor, Private Pike in the British sitcom Dad's Army

explanation.surface: A lavender plant is set in the battlefield for a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lavender' looks like the plant, but it is the actor Ian Lavender.
explanation.definitionFit: Marianne is a female given name, and so a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: Song writer's first to enter abbey

indicators.note: to enter puts the chosen letter inside the abbey's name

parts.note: Downton Abbey is the British TV period drama set in a country house

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of writer is taken

explanation.surface: A songwriter is the first to go into a monastery.
explanation.walkthrough: W, the first letter of writer, goes inside DOWNTON; 'Song writer' looks like one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the 1964 hit by Petula Clark, a famous pop single.

clue.text: Art of jazz — change backing endlessly

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the trimmed word is read backwards
endlessly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to mutate is to change

explanation.surface: The art of jazz lies in reversing change without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' looks like the abstract noun but is Art Tatum: MUTATE loses its end (endlessly) to make MUTAT, which read backwards (backing) is the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Tatum was a celebrated American jazz pianist of extraordinary technique.

clue.text: About one degree Fahrenheit — sign for actress

indicators.note: about means going around, so the degree letters surround the one

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree
I is the Roman numeral for one
an arrow is a sign pointing the way

explanation.surface: Roughly one degree on a thermometer is a sign for a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mia Farrow is an American film actress, star of Rosemary's Baby.

clue.text: Worried composer accepts one-note instrument

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the jumbled letters hold the other pieces
worried means agitated, signalling the letters are shaken up

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: An anxious composer takes on an instrument that plays a single note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one-note instrument' suggests music, but the instrument is scientific; Worried rearranges COMPOSER to MROSCOPE, which takes in I and C.
explanation.definitionFit: A microscope is an optical instrument for magnifying tiny objects.

clue.text: Don't eat such food from a takeaway

definitions.meaning: to go without food, as on a religious day of abstinence
quick food bought at a takeaway is called by this word plus food

explanation.surface: Advice to avoid eating junk bought at a takeaway.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is going without food; the other is the word before food for burgers and chips.

clue.text: Tell singer to provide dish

parts.note: to peach on someone is to inform on them, to tell
Dame Nellie Melba was an Australian operatic soprano

explanation.surface: Someone is told to have a vocalist serve a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The dessert was in fact created by Escoffier in honour of Nellie Melba.
explanation.definitionFit: A peach melba is a dessert of peaches, ice cream and raspberry sauce.

clue.text: Wow! Folk learn new song — possibly

indicators.note: new means made afresh, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Amazement as some people pick up a fresh tune.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also a song title, which 'song' hints at; the phrase itself means perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to mean perhaps, as far as anyone can tell.

clue.text: Sea mail at sea with no exceptions

indicators.note: at sea means confused or adrift, signalling the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Post sent by ship goes astray without any exceptions.
explanation.definitionFit: Anomalies are deviations from the norm, things that do not fit the rule.

clue.text: Carol's invitees? True, but 7 would need another 50

definitions.meaning: the carol O Come, All Ye ... invites the believers to come
true in the sense of loyal and steadfast

explanation.surface: A carol's guests are loyal, but a singer would need an extra letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The tail is a joke: 7 is MARIANNE, and the singer Marianne Faithfull needs another L, the Roman numeral for 50.
explanation.definitionFit: The carol summons believers, who are loyal ones; the adjective means steadfast and loyal.

clue.text: Record producers? One's in Tardis after doctoring

indicators.note: in puts the pieces for one's inside the rearranged letters
doctoring means tampering with, so the letters of the time machine are altered

parts.note: I is one and the 's gives S

explanation.surface: Someone climbs into the Doctor's time machine after it has been tampered with.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tardis is Doctor Who's time machine, so 'doctoring' is a pun; it rearranges TARDIS to DIARTS, which takes in IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Diarists produce written records of their days, so they are record producers, not music people.

clue.text: Song from one who's intended to entertain 24 getting married — certainly not 24 in service

parts.note: A means one, as in a single thing

indicators.note: to entertain means to host, so the intended one holds the other pieces

parts.note: a fiancé is someone's intended spouse
the answer to 24-down, the emperor who fiddled
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A tune from a betrothed person who hosts an emperor and weds.
explanation.walkthrough: The tail is a second cryptic reading: Nero was certainly not A FINE ROMAN, and that sits before CE, the Church of England service.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Jerome Kern and Dorothy Fields standard, sung by Fred Astaire.

clue.text: Middle section of serenade? Play it again!

indicators.note: section of here picks out the central pair of letters of the love song word

parts.note: the core is the middle of something

explanation.surface: Asking for the central part of a love song to be performed once more.
explanation.walkthrough: EN is the very middle of SERENADE, and CORE is middle, giving the call for another performance.
explanation.definitionFit: An encore is a call for a repeat performance at the end of a show.

clue.text: See 1
Mormon's last seen by salt lake

indicators.note: seen by means placed beside, joining the pieces

parts.note: an old salt is a sailor, as is a tar

indicators.note: last means the final letter of Mormon

explanation.surface: A Mormon's final view by the Great Salt Lake of Utah.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt lake' suggests Utah, but salt is the sailor and lake is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarn is a small mountain lake, especially in northern England.

clue.text: Rolling Stone with first-class stuff in US city

indicators.note: in puts the other pieces into the rolled letters
rolling means tumbling about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: A, as in A1, means first-class
to cram is to stuff

explanation.surface: A Rolling Stone with top-quality material in some American town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling Stone' reads as the band; Rolling turns STONE into SENTO, into which A and CRAM go.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacramento is the state capital of California.

clue.text: Very strict cook, marginally improved

parts.note: to cook the books is to rig or fiddle them

indicators.note: marginally means only the edges of the word are kept

explanation.surface: A very strict chef, only slightly better.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigid means inflexible, so very strict rules are rigid ones.

clue.text: Fiddler, it's said, turned on when hugging the leading lady

indicators.note: hugging means holding inside, so the turned word goes round the lady
turned means turned round, so the little word is read backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, is the first lady of the land

explanation.surface: A violinist is said to be aroused when embracing the star actress.
explanation.walkthrough: Nero is said to have fiddled while Rome burned, hence 'it's said'; ON turned is NO, hugging ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says the emperor played the fiddle while Rome burned.

clue.text: Jodie heads for island, needing gentle care

parts.note: Jodie Foster is an American film actress

indicators.note: heads for means the first letters of the next words

explanation.surface: An actress makes for an island, needing gentle treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Fostering is bringing up a child not your own, providing care.

clue.text: Divers in Amarillo on springboards

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Swimmers in a Texas city use the springboards.
explanation.definitionFit: In North America the diving bird called a diver in Britain is a loon.

clue.text: Teaching the children in franglais?

parts.note: les is the French for the
sons are male children

explanation.surface: Instruction for the kids in a French and English mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in franglais' tells you to mix French and English: the French word for the, then an English word for children.
explanation.definitionFit: Lessons are periods of teaching or instruction.

clue.text: Year-end frolics in clergyman's home

indicators.note: frolics means plays about, signalling a jumble of the letters

explanation.surface: End-of-year parties at the vicar's house.
explanation.definitionFit: A deanery is the official residence of a dean.
